record.paper_title: Chebyshev Sets, Klee Sets, and Chebyshev Centers with respect to Bregman Distances: Recent Results and Open Problems
record.context_brief: Existence of nonquadratic full-domain right D-Chebyshev geometry
record.original_question: Let X = R^n, let f: X -> [-infinity, +infinity] be a convex Legendre function with full domain X, and define the Bregman distance D(a, b) = f(a) - f(b) - <grad f(b), a - b>. A nonempty closed convex subset C of X is right D-Chebyshev if every x in X has a unique point y in C minimizing D(x, y). Does there exist such an f that is not quadratic, but for which every nonempty closed convex subset of X is right D-Chebyshev? Equivalently, can a nonquadratic full-domain Legendre generator have a nonaffine gradient map that nevertheless preserves convexity strongly enough to make all nonempty closed convex subsets right D-Chebyshev?

evidence.quote: Fact 3.4 (See [6, Lemma 3.5].) Suppose that f is the negative entropy (see Example 1.1(ii)) and that C is convex. Then C is ->D-Chebyshev.

Fact 3.4 raises two intriguing questions. Apart from the case of quadratic functions, are there instances of f where f has full domain and where every closed convex subset of U is ->D-Chebyshev? Because of Fact 3.2, an affirmative answer to this question would imply that grad f is a (quite surprising) nonaffine yet convexity-preserving transformation.

Problem 3. Does there exist a Legendre function f with full domain such that f is not quadratic yet every nonempty closed convex subset of X is ->D-Chebyshev? In view of Fact 3.1, the gradient operator grad f of such a function would be nonaffine and it would preserve convexity.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let X = R^n with the standard inner product ⟨·,·⟩. A function f: X → (−∞, +∞] is called a convex function of Legendre type with full domain X if:
(i) dom f = X, f is convex, lower semicontinuous, and essentially smooth in the sense that f is differentiable on X with ∇f continuous; and
(ii) f is essentially strictly convex, equivalently, ∇f is injective on X (so that ∇f: X → ∇f(X) is a bijection onto an open convex set with ∇f^{-1} = ∇f*, where f* denotes the Fenchel conjugate of f).

For such f, define the Bregman distance
   D(a, b) = f(a) − f(b) − ⟨∇f(b), a − b⟩, for a, b ∈ X.

A nonempty closed convex subset C ⊆ X is called right D-Chebyshev if, for every x ∈ X, there exists a unique point y = y(x) ∈ C minimizing the function y ↦ D(x, y) over C (i.e., the second argument is the variable point in C).

Question: Does there exist a convex Legendre function f: X → R with full domain X which is not a quadratic function (equivalently, whose gradient map ∇f is not affine), yet for which every nonempty closed convex subset C of X is right D-Chebyshev?

Note: An affirmative answer would produce a nonaffine yet convexity-preserving smooth bijection ∇f of X onto an open convex subset of X.

status_evidence.title: Chebyshev Sets, Klee Sets, and Chebyshev Centers with Respect to Bregman Distances: Recent Results and Open Problems
status_evidence.snippet: Survey reviewing known results and presenting open problems on Chebyshev sets and related notions with respect to Bregman distances.
status_evidence.claim: The problem is listed as an explicit open problem in this survey.

status_evidence.title: Klee sets and Chebyshev centers for the right Bregman distance
status_evidence.snippet: Studies right Bregman distance Klee sets and Chebyshev centers but does not resolve the nonquadratic full-domain right D-Chebyshev question.
status_evidence.claim: Adjacent results in the literature do not resolve the posed problem.

status_evidence.title: On Bregman-Type Distances and Their Associated Projection Mappings
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses Bregman-type projections and convexity; no announcement of resolving the nonaffine convexity-preserving gradient problem.
status_evidence.claim: Later work on Bregman projections does not solve the problem.
